topic: What trade-offs exist between reflector aperture size and feed element redundancy in robust antenna design?
consensus_response: The trade-off between reflector aperture size and feed element redundancy lies in the physical mechanism of array factor and interference patterns. Increasing reflector aperture size leads to higher directivity but also more pronounced interference patterns due to unit cell loss, compromising efficiency (4.95 dB at 2 dB). Conversely, incorporating redundant feed elements enhances robustness by mitigating pattern shape instability in case of feed element failures. The defocused reflector concept can improve pattern shape stability in case of feed element failures, making it a promising approach for robust antenna design.
